chunk_1.page_content:
Interface Requirements Specification (IRS)

Sample Network Packet Definitions

Document ID: IRS-SAMPLE-002

Version: 1.1

Purpose: Define three illustrative network packet formats for packet-schema extraction and validation.

chunk_2.page_content:
# 1 Introduction

This document specifies three distinct network packet formats. The functional packet requirements and field layouts are defined in Section 3.

chunk_4.page_content:
## 2.1 Numeric Representation

Unless a packet requirement states otherwise, multi-byte numeric values shall use big-endian byte order.

chunk_5.page_content:
## 2.2 Text Representation

ASCII string fields shall contain ASCII characters. Fixed-width ASCII fields shall be padded with NULL bytes when the supplied text is shorter than the specified field width.

chunk_6.page_content:
## 2.3 Field Ordering and Sizes

Fields shall appear in the order listed in their packet's field-layout subsection. All sizes are expressed in bytes. A variable-length field shall be identified explicitly as variable-length.

chunk_7.page_content:
# 3 Functional Requirements

This section defines the three packet types supported by this sample interface. Each packet has its own numbered subsections and field-layout requirements.

chunk_9.page_content:
### 3.1.1 Packet Overview

The Sample Packet shall have a fixed total length of 34 bytes. The packet shall contain five fields in the order specified in Section 3.1.2.

chunk_10.page_content:
### 3.1.2 Field Layout
Field Name Data Type / Encoding Size (bytes) Requirement
Header ASCII 6 The field shall contain the literal value "SAMPLE".
Name ASCII string 20 The field shall be padded with NULL bytes when shorter than 20 bytes.
Age Unsigned 8-bit integer 1 The field shall represent the person's age as an unsigned integer.
Roll Number Unsigned 8-bit integer 1 The field shall represent the roll number as an unsigned integer.
Footer ASCII 6 The field shall contain the literal value "FOOTER".

chunk_11.page_content:
### 3.1.3 Packet Length Validation

A receiver shall accept a Sample Packet only when its total length is exactly 34 bytes. The sum of its field sizes shall be 6 + 20 + 1 + 1 + 6 = 34 bytes.

chunk_13.page_content:
### 3.2.1 Packet Overview

The Telemetry Packet shall have a fixed total length of 31 bytes. It shall contain exactly six fields in the order specified in Section 3.2.2.

chunk_14.page_content:
### 3.2.2 Field Layout
Field Name Data Type / Encoding Size (bytes) Requirement
Device ID Unsigned 16-bit integer 2 The field shall identify the transmitting device.
Sequence Number Unsigned 32-bit integer 4 The field shall contain the packet sequence number.
Temperature IEEE 754 float32 4 The field shall contain the measured temperature in degrees Celsius.
Alarm Active Boolean 1 The value shall be 0 for inactive or 1 for active.
Device Label ASCII string 12 The field shall be a fixed-width, NULL-padded device label.
Timestamp Unsigned 64-bit integer 8 The field shall contain a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

chunk_15.page_content:
### 3.2.3 Numeric Encoding and Packet Length

All multi-byte numeric fields in the Telemetry Packet shall use big-endian byte order. The Boolean field shall occupy exactly one byte. A receiver shall accept this packet only when its total length is exactly 31 bytes. The sum of its field sizes shall be 2 + 4 + 4 + 1 + 12 + 8 = 31 bytes.

chunk_17.page_content:
### 3.3.1 Packet Overview

The Variable Payload Packet shall contain exactly one field. The packet has no fixed total length.

chunk_18.page_content:
### 3.3.2 Field Layout
Field Name Data Type / Encoding Size (bytes) Requirement
Payload Raw bytes Variable (1–1024) The field shall contain between 1 and 1024 bytes and shall occupy the entire packet body.

chunk_19.page_content:
### 3.3.3 Variable-Length and Packet Boundary Requirements

The Payload field shall have a minimum length of 1 byte and a maximum length of 1024 bytes. Its end shall be determined by the end of the packet as provided by the enclosing transport or framing mechanism. No fixed total packet size or separate length-prefix field is defined. A receiver shall reject a payload shorter than 1 byte or longer than 1024 bytes.

chunk_21.page_content:
## 4.1 Sample Packet

Required packet length: exactly 34 bytes.

chunk_22.page_content:
## 4.2 Telemetry Packet

Required packet length: exactly 31 bytes.

chunk_23.page_content:
## 4.3 Variable Payload Packet

Required payload length: 1 to 1024 bytes; total packet length is variable.

chunk_24.page_content:
# 5 Document Notes

This is a synthetic training document intended for testing IRS extraction and packet validation workflows. It does not define a production network protocol.
